decisions.why: FR-001 verbatim: the field, when to give one, process-fault always carries its fault, no 'file a tooling row'. The refusal on a process-fault without the field only enforces FR-001. 'Whenever the loop came from a tooling gap' is a floor (must give one then), not a ceiling; the contract must keep FR-001's 'never only in its prose' for any tooling fix the arbiter recommends, or an incidental one is lost again. The accept line's 'filed as rows' concerns finding rows, not tooling rows, and FR-001 does not reach it. decisions.summary: The open-task refusal is not touched (no flag); make land-tooling FILES= builds a new commit on the latest main holding only FILES' committed changes since the merge base (git diff base HEAD -- FILES, git apply --index, a failure being 'does not apply cleanly'), in a detached worktree at .clones/<clone>-tooling, landed by the sync script's stop-work step run from the worktree so every push check runs; clone history untouched; worktree removed on every exit.
decisions.why: FR-005: the tooling lands on main by itself, on top of the latest main, through a push's checks, no history rewritten, no local branch, while the feature's other work stays in the clone (the refusal is meant to keep holding it - SC-003 'the full push is still refused'). The request's 'a commit that touches only tooling land on its own' is the accepted spec's 'lands a commit's TOOLING'; a new commit of that tooling on main is that, not less. Measured premises checked: .specify/feature.json is gitignored (.gitignore:124, not in ls-files), and the sync script derives the active feature only from touched specs/ and that pointer (lines 415-422) and checks only that its root is under .clones/ (line 65), so the push from the worktree finds no feature in progress. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) Naming the files withholds nothing the GM asked to land: any tooling path may be named, and the no-FILES case prints the compliant command. 'Only committed work' is FR-005's 'a commit's tooling'. Running each landed test before the push is FR-005's 'any test it lands is run there ... refused rather than breaking main' and SC-003's last clause; hooks-test and tests/tooling are the checks this project owes a tooling change before it lands (Constitution XIII, the plan's own constitution check) and enforce 'rather than breaking main', so they serve the request rather than add scope. Regenerating make-targets.html is the wiring FR-005 names. decisions.summary: hm_review_round.py: a spec review's round past SPEC_ROUND_CAP=5 plus the continue rulings on THIS PASS (round:spec-fidelity|<feature>#<pass>@) trips @N and refuses before the snapshot moves; the pass advances when a dispatch follows an ACCEPTED pass - a FAITHFUL round, or the arbiter's accept or process-fault on that pass (ruled_closed); ARBITER_OK escape. Amendment 3: a REVIEW_ROUND_OK full re-read after an ACCEPTED pass also starts the new pass at round 1 (accepted_pass).
decisions.why: Within. The pass advancing on FAITHFUL or on the arbiter's accept/process-fault is FR-007's 'counter reset when a spec is accepted or amended'; ARBITER_OK follows the pair-hooks precedent FR-007 names. Amendment 3's added note: the escape path now does what the routed path already did - accepted_pass() resets to round 1 and advances the pass only when the last pass ended FAITHFUL (transcript, else the Review history) or closed by an arbiter accept/process-fault; otherwise it keeps the round as before. That is FR-007's reset applied to the one path that skipped it (amendment 3's own first round had counted as round 4 of a finished pass), neither lifting a cap mid-pass nor adding one. Test: tests/hooks/test-review-round-hooks.sh section 10 (round 3 + FAITHFUL + escape -> round 1, pass 3). Round 3's note (b) stands as an aside.

decisions.summary: An arbiter accept/process-fault answers review-gate.sh in place of FAITHFUL only while spec.md's title and its sections up to the Review history hash as when ruled (header block dropped whole); a continue does not.
decisions.why: Round 4's item resolved. spec_body_sha now hashes the title line plus everything from the first '## ' heading to the Review history, the header block between dropped whole (head.split('\n',1)[0] + sep + rest). MEASURED on round 5's own run, 2026-10-10: on a copy of 379's own spec.md, Status rewritten to a Done that wraps onto a second line keeps the hash (True); a one-word FR-007 edit changes it (False). tests/hooks/test-review-gate.sh: 38 passed 0 failed (b4's new two-line Status case among them); tests/tooling/test_arbiter_fix.py: 9 passed (the spec-ruling test now writes a wrapped Status and keeps the ruling; the requirement edit still cancels). The remaining narrowing - a requirement edit cancels the ruling - is LEGITIMATE: implied by FR-007's own 'counter reset when a spec is accepted or amended' (an amended spec owes a new review, not an old ruling), and it applies to the requirements only, so an arbiter-accepted feature lands with its Status rewritten (D12's own purpose). Aside, not a finding: a spec with no '## ' heading hashes its title alone (3 of the repository's specs, all filed/withdrawn/done stubs: 275, 325, 373), so a body edit there keeps a ruling - that is looser, never stricter, than the request, and the FAITHFUL path (a grep over spec.md) is not content-bound at all. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: make perf-arbiter [ENV=] takes subject perf-band3-<env>-<first 12 of binding(commit, environment, measurements)> from perf_review.py arbiter-subject (band 3 only) and runs make arbiter-ask, writing perf_review show's report beside the MANIFEST; perf_review.check counts an arbiter accept on ask:<that subject> in the feature's arbiter.jsonl as the band-3 record; continue, process-fault and other numbers do not; the MISSING line names perf-arbiter alone, 'never a question to the GM'; signoff stays only for a sign-off the GM gives unprompted, its no-terminal refusal naming the arbiter; the arbiter's contract states the standard it rules by (the band-2 criteria, held strictest); every FR-011 text says the arbiter; the session memory is rewritten.
decisions.why: FR-011 clause by clause. 'One command that records the question and builds its bundle, the perf report in it': perf-arbiter chains arbiter-ask (hm_arbiter ask + arbiter_bundle) and writes perf-report.txt to /tmp/l7r-check/arbiter-ask-<subject>, which is the bundle's own directory (arbiter_bundle slug of 'ask:perf-band3-...' is 'ask-perf-band3-...', 37 chars, under its 60 cut). 'An accept bound to that bookend pair's exact numbers': the subject is the pair's existing binding (sha256 of commit, environment, measurements), so new numbers mean a new trigger. 'continue and process-fault do not; a ruling on other numbers is stale': arbiter_signed matches ruling == accept on the exact trigger only; tests/tools/test_perf_review.py test_band_3_goes_to_the_round_arbiter_first covers continue, other numbers and accept. 'The push's refusal names that command alone': the MISSING line names make perf-arbiter and not perf-signoff (asserted). 'A sign-off the GM gives unprompted still counts': signoff --tty yes still records and passes check (test_band_3_a_GM_signoff_given_unprompted_is_still_recorded). The push wiring reaches it: sync-with-main runs make perf-review, i.e. check with --specs-dir defaulting to the repository's specs/, and record_ruling writes the accept into the active feature's tracked arbiter.jsonl, the file arbiter_signed reads. Giving the arbiter a standard to rule by narrows nothing the GM asked: FR-011 puts the decision to the arbiter, and a stated standard is how it decides; the GM reviews every ruling after landing. 'Only band 3 has a subject' is FR-011's scope (band 3 only). The memory rewrite serves 'the session NEVER asks the GM'.
